candidate.claim: Restricting to periodic antisymmetric functions yields an explicit Fourier basis in which the RH closure condition becomes convergence of arithmetic coordinate sequences.
candidate.proposed_limit: The smaller space preserves the criterion only because the coefficient-correction argument is proved; arbitrary symmetry restriction would not.
candidate.title: Symmetry compression makes Nyman-Beurling computational

parents.context_note: The family is not complete in the ambient Hilbert space, motivating the restricted space HP.
parents.representation_dependency: Displayed integrals are readable with moderate OCR risk.
parents.selection_reason: Evaluates the weighted sine-product integral by a min formula and uses four cancellations to prove orthonormality, then defines the two symmetry constraints of the closed span.
parents.title: Adjacent sine differences form an orthonormal family

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The adjacent sine differences E_n are tailored to the weighted sine-product kernel. That kernel evaluates to a multiple of min(p,q); expanding the inner product of two adjacent differences produces four neighboring min terms that cancel off the diagonal and leave one on it. Period-one and reflection-antisymmetry conditions then identify HP as the natural subspace in which this orthonormal family is stated to be complete, while it is explicitly incomplete in the ambient H.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Recognizes adjacent differencing as the discrete operation that diagonalizes the min kernel and links completeness to a symmetry-selected subspace.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted as a precise, critic-approved mechanism rather than a generic Fourier analogy.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span defines E_n, proves the min-kernel lemma and four-term orthonormality, defines HP by two symmetries, and states the basis theorem there. Integral normalizations have moderate OCR risk.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. Completeness is attributed only to HP and is merely stated, not reproved, in this unit.

parents.context_note: The transformation is an isometric isomorphism and makes coordinates explicit.
parents.representation_dependency: The weight-folding formulas are dense but the Fourier conclusion is prose-supported.
parents.selection_reason: Proves completeness in HP by folding the weighted norm to the unit interval, multiplying by a sine factor, and identifying the transformed basis with the canonical odd-frequency cosine basis.
parents.title: Periodic antisymmetry turns HP into an odd-cosine Fourier space

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The completeness proof folds the weighted half-line onto one period, uses reflection antisymmetry to combine the folded contributions, and absorbs the resulting sine-squared weight into an isometric multiplier. Under this map, the specialized E_n become the standard odd-frequency cosine basis. The two original symmetries eliminate sine and even-cosine modes, so Parseval transfers ordinary Fourier completeness back to HP without asserting completeness in all of H.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies a norm-preserving representation in which the unfamiliar basis and its lost modes become standard Fourier data.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the critic confirmed every step of the representation change and boundary.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span performs the norm folding, defines the isometry, displays the vanishing modes, maps E_n to odd cosines, and concludes with Parseval. The exact square-root and sine factors need scan checking.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. The dependence on both symmetries and the restriction to HP are explicit.

parents.context_note: The correction uses symmetry to control the sum of coefficients, making the smaller-space formulation exact rather than merely sufficient.
parents.representation_dependency: Prose fixes the equivalence; a few norms and coefficient sums are formula-sensitive.
parents.selection_reason: Transfers the standard Nyman-Beurling/Baez-Duarte statement through a known isometry and proves that any fractional-part approximation can be corrected to one using eq(t)={qt}-{t} without losing convergence.
parents.title: RH is equivalent to approximating E1 by fractional-part differences inside HP

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The restriction from fractional-part generators {qt} in H to difference generators e_q={qt}-{t} in HP is justified by a quantitative correction. Pairing an approximation error at t and 1-t bounds the total coefficient sum; adding that small sum times {t} converts the approximant to e_q generators while preserving convergence. The smaller-space criterion is therefore equivalent to the known RH approximation criterion because the symmetry-violating component is controlled, not merely discarded.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies and bounds the exact component lost by changing generator families, thereby auditing why the restriction preserves rather than strengthens the closure statement.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted as critic-approved because the concrete correction mechanism carries the conceptual claim.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The unit transports the Nyman-Beurling/Baez-Duarte criterion by an isometry and proves the reverse restriction using the reflection identity, coefficient-sum bound, and corrected errors. Constants are formula-sensitive.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. Rational-point exceptions are null at the L2 level, and membership alone is not treated as proving equivalence.

parents.context_note: This is the core representation change from functions to explicit arithmetic sequences.
parents.representation_dependency: The integration-by-parts chain is OCR-dense; endpoint formula is clear.
parents.selection_reason: Computes the exact coordinates of each eq by converting fractional-part integrals into harmonic sums over p/q at most k below p, enabling all later approximation calculations.
parents.title: A basis coordinate is a logarithm minus a short harmonic interval

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The inner product of E_p with e_q collapses from an infinite weighted fractional-part integral to log q minus a finite harmonic sum over the half-open interval p/q <= k < p. This changes the approximation problem from functions to explicit arithmetic coordinates. The interval incidence gives the coordinate array a triangular structure that later Moebius cancellation can exploit, while the endpoint convention remains essential for exact cancellation.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Extracts the discrete incidence structure hidden in the analytic inner product and states what it enables without claiming norm convergence.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the critic confirmed the formula-to-arithmetic representation change and its precise limitation.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span derives the coordinate by partitioning, rescaling, summing sine terms, and integrating by parts, ending with the stated logarithm-minus-harmonic formula. The derivation is OCR-dense but the endpoint formula is clear.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. The identity supplies entries of the approximation problem only; convergence remains a separate burden.

candidate.claim: All three approximations hit every fixed coordinate asymptotically and have controlled far tails, so their unresolved content is exactly uniform square-summable domination on a moving finite range.
candidate.proposed_limit: None of the three unconditional analyses supplies that dominator; treating fixed-coordinate convergence as sufficient would be invalid.
candidate.title: Coordinatewise convergence is not Hilbert-space convergence

parents.context_note: The finite exact cancellation motivates both the coefficient choice and the later natural approximation.
parents.representation_dependency: Coefficient formulas are extraction-sensitive but the cancellation system is recoverable.
parents.selection_reason: Uses Moebius-weighted coefficients plus two boundary corrections to solve a triangular coordinate system, leaving an explicit tail beginning at n+1 and proving every fixed coordinate has the target limit.
parents.title: Finite coefficients cancel the first n basis errors exactly

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The triangular construction uses Moebius-weighted interior coefficients and two terminal corrections. Divisor cancellation plus two scalar equations force the first n basis coordinates to equal the target coordinates exactly, leaving an explicit error supported only on indices p >= n+1. This is finite interpolation, not Hilbert convergence: even if every fixed coordinate eventually vanishes, norm mass may move outward, so a uniform square-summable tail dominator is still required.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates exact finite-coordinate cancellation from moving-tail control and explains the distinct jobs of Moebius interior terms and boundary repairs.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted because the critic approved the triangular mechanism and its central unresolved global obligation.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The unit defines the coefficients, proves the divisor identity, solves the two boundary equations, and expands the residual tail from n+1. Signs and terminal formulas are extraction-sensitive, while the cancellation structure is recoverable.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. Coordinatewise convergence is not promoted to norm convergence.

parents.context_note: Coordinatewise convergence alone is insufficient; this criterion makes the missing domination precise.
parents.representation_dependency: Asymptotic symbols are slightly degraded; range and mechanism are explicit.
parents.selection_reason: Proves a far-tail bound of order n squared over p log n and isolates the only uncontrolled indices, n+1 through n to the fourth, where a common square-summable bound along infinitely many n would imply RH.
parents.title: The triangular tail reduces RH to uniform control on a moving intermediate range

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Euler-Maclaurin estimates give x_{n,p}=O(n^2/(p log n)), and for p at least n^4 this supplies the stated square-summable far-tail comparison. Combined with fixed-coordinate convergence, the estimate localizes the uncontrolled norm mass to the moving window n+1 through n^4. The artifact begins a domination condition on that window but ends before its quantifier and conclusion, so this unit alone does not certify an RH criterion.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Partitions the error into fixed, intermediate, and far-tail regimes and identifies which regime remains uncontrolled, while auditing the missing logical conclusion.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after the critic's correction because the proved tail localization is useful and the incomplete criterion is explicitly bounded rather than reconstructed.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The unit proves the asymptotic decay, derives the far-tail bound, and displays the intermediate-range inequality before the semantic boundary cuts the criterion. Exact asymptotic glyphs are mildly degraded.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. Any claim about infinitely many n or implication to RH is withheld because it lies outside the frozen span.

parents.context_note: The source calls these simultaneous conditions difficult and invokes a square-root Omega obstruction for the summatory Moebius function.
parents.representation_dependency: The exact squared-norm identity is formula-heavy; its stated consequence is prose-supported.
parents.selection_reason: Proves the natural Moebius approximation has the right coordinate limits and a controllable far tail, states its RH criterion, then computes the low-mode squared mass and shows domination would require simultaneous strong bounds on two Moebius sums.
parents.title: Moebius/q coefficients converge coordinatewise but force restrictive low-mode sums

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The natural coefficients mu(q)/q give the correct limit in every fixed basis coordinate and an O(n/p) estimate controlling the far tail. The exact squared-mass identity for modes two through n+1 then shows where the difficulty remains: two explicit summatory Moebius quantities must satisfy simultaneous restrictive bounds. Thus local divisor algebra and far-tail decay coexist with a potentially large moving low-frequency block; the source calls the needed joint behavior difficult but does not prove it.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Uses Parseval-style mode separation to diagnose the exact arithmetic quantities controlling the unresolved norm, without importing the missing Omega theorem.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after applying the critic's boundary correction; the central moving-block obstruction is fully visible in the unit.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The unit proves fixed-coordinate limits, the O(n/p) bound, states a square-summable domination criterion, computes the low-mode norm identity, and derives the simultaneous inequalities. It ends before the promised external obstruction.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. The simultaneous bounds remain unproved, and neither an Omega statement nor an RH-conditional rate from adjacent context is included.

parents.context_note: The paper establishes the criterion as sufficient; the cited converse-rate result under RH does not itself furnish an unconditional proof.
parents.representation_dependency: The epsilon glyph is corrupted in extraction but assumptions and tail estimates are recoverable.
parents.selection_reason: Adds q to the minus-epsilon damping, chooses epsilon at least twice log log n over log n, controls the omitted Dirichlet-series tails directly, and states a square-summable criterion known under RH to hold for a slower explicit epsilon.
parents.title: A vanishing exponent regularizes the Moebius tail without changing coordinate limits

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Replacing mu(q)/q by mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n) introduces a bias that vanishes on fixed coordinates while making the omitted reciprocal-zeta Dirichlet tails directly estimable. The lower bound on epsilon_n prevents smoothing from disappearing too quickly, and epsilon_n tending to zero preserves the target local limit; the O(n/p) far-tail control remains. This improves truncation regularity but does not finish the argument, because Criterion 3 still assumes an unproved common square-summable dominator on the remaining range.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies the exact bias-versus-tail tradeoff and separates absolute truncation control from the still-missing Hilbert-norm domination.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after the critic-mandated removal because the mechanism and remaining obligation are source-clear despite glyph corruption.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span gives the smoothed coefficients, the recoverable lower and vanishing conditions on epsilon_n, direct tail estimates, fixed-coordinate limits, far-tail bound, and domination criterion. The epsilon glyph is corrupted, and the final Balazard result is cut off.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation. The uncontained Balazard/RH rate claim is deleted, and smoothing is not presented as solving the criterion.

candidate.claim: Boundary-corrected coefficients annihilate initial modes, pure Moebius coefficients simplify the construction but expose restrictive summatory behavior, and a small exponent damps the arithmetic tail while preserving the limit.
candidate.proposed_limit: Smoothing improves the criterion's plausibility and conditional rate but remains tied to unproved uniform bounds.
candidate.title: Exact cancellation, natural coefficients, and smoothing trade local error against arithmetic regularity
